findings.what: Nine of the twelve catalogue facts have NO correction path once answered, and a skipped item can never be answered later — although the shipped copy promises exactly that and the database door supports both. The brief closes C48.5 here on "persisted answers, applicability and correction path"; the final report claims "applicability + correction path on the facts panel", but the facts panel only reaches knowledge records, i.e. the three D8 keys.
findings.evidence: checklist.tsx:456 gates every write control on `!committed && isPending(item)`, and `isPending` is `state === "pending"` (types.ts:145-147). The group walk is filtered the same way (checklist.tsx:316) and `setOpen({kind:"item"})` is only reachable from that same gated button, so an `answered`/`resolved`/`deferred` item has no Answer, no Change and no un-skip control anywhere on the page. `FirmConfirmedFactsPanel` (checklist.tsx:518) renders `env.confirmed_facts`, which `clara.get_firm_setup` builds from `clara.knowledge_records` joined to the catalogue (0203_firm_setup.sql:1057-1061) — only `currency`, `framework`, `accounting_basis`. So `legal_name`, `ssm`, `entity_type`, `address`, `mia`, `turnover`, `tin`, `fye`, `mpers_eligibility` are write-once from this surface. apps/web/messages/en.json `FirmSetup.skip.description` says "It does not hold up finishing setup, and you can answer it later." — there is no control that can. The door is not the limit: on the fresh rig, `clara.answer_firm_setup_item` accepted a re-answer of an item whose record had been withdrawn (probe1 P7: "P7 re-answer after withdraw -> ACCEPTED"), and 0203:786-789 sets `state='answered'` from any non-committed state.
findings.fix: Render a write control for settled items: for a plan-only item (`knowledge_key === null`) an "Answer again"/"Change" button that opens the same `FirmSetupItemForm` prefilled with `answerText(item)`; for a deferred item the same button labelled "Answer this now"; for the three captured keys keep pointing at the facts panel, since the door's `knowledge_already_live` already has a designed face (`form.alreadyLive`). Add two red-first cells: (a) `firm-setup-checklist.test.tsx` — a deferred item exposes an answer control and the submit reaches `answer_firm_setup_item`; (b) `packages/db/tests/firm-setup.test.mjs` — `defer` then `answer` the same item leaves it `answered` with the new value and the deferral reason gone.

findings.what: The lost-response recovery the brief names ("re-read `get_firm_setup` before offering a distinct resubmit, same op_key for a retry") provably cannot work against the real door. `_reserve_op`'s request hash includes `p_expected_revision`, and the surface reloads the envelope before offering the retry, so the retry always carries a DIFFERENT hash under the SAME op key and is refused `CLR10 "op_key reused with different args"` — a raw, unmapped message painted beside the control, next to "The database refused this value", when in fact the answer was accepted. The only test covering this (`fs.web.06`) passes because its mock returns a frozen envelope whose revision never rotates.
findings.evidence: Probe on the fresh rig (55607/clara_648r), exactly reproducing the browser sequence answer→lost ack→`loadFirmSetup`→press Save again with the same derived key: `L1 lost-response retry (write HAD landed) -> CLR10 "op_key reused with different args" detail=<none>`. Same class inside one walk: `L2 re-submitting an ALREADY-LANDED step of the same walk -> CLR10 "op_key reused with different args"`. `classify` (checklist.tsx:137-160) has no arm for that message (no `detail.reason`), so it falls through to `kind:"invalid"`; `firm-setup-item-form.tsx:195-199,256-257` then sets `problems[...]="server"` and renders `outcome.message` verbatim. en.json `FirmSetup.form.failed` asserts "pressing Save again sends the same request rather than answering twice". The fix is proven on the same rig: retrying with the op key AND the revision that was actually sent replays the receipt with no second effect — `F2 fix — retry with the ORIGINALLY SENT revision -> receipt replayed: "legal_name"` / `receipts: 2 | plan revision_n: 4`.
findings.fix: Keep the exact request that was sent (op key + `expectedRevision` + answer) in the form's state on a transport failure, and resend that same triple on the retry instead of the freshly reloaded token — `_reserve_op` short-circuits before the CAS check (0203:757-760 precedes :765-770), so the stale token is never evaluated and the receipt replays. Also map the bare `CLR10 "op_key reused with different args"` to its own face ("this answer was already recorded — the checklist has been re-read"). Re-point `fs.web.06` so the mock rotates `revision_token` on the first (lost) write, which is what makes it a real test.

findings.what: The op key is a pure function of (verb, plan, item_key, value), so it is stable across TIME, not across one attempt. Any intent that was ever submitted can never be submitted again: the key matches an existing receipt while the payload hash (which carries the current revision) does not, so the door refuses `CLR10 "op_key reused with different args"` permanently. Today F1 hides this for answers; the moment F1's change control lands, "A → B → back to A" is a dead end, and `defer` already carries the same defect (its key is f(verb, plan, item_key, reason), so skipping an item with a reason ever used before is refused).
findings.evidence: Probe on 55607/clara_648r with the exact `firmSetupOpKey` derivation: `P1 revert-to-earlier-value -> CLR10 "op_key reused with different args" detail=<none> | item still: "MIA-2"` — the earlier value can never be restored. Same-key/different-payload is a typed refusal and same-key/same-payload correctly replays one receipt (`P2 same-key/diff-payload -> CLR10 … | same-key/same-payload replay -> receipt replayed | receipts: 1`), so the door is behaving; the client's key derivation is the defect.
findings.fix: Mint a fresh op key when a form is opened or its value is edited (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()` held in form state), and reuse it only for an explicit retry of that same attempt — which is the same state F2's fix already has to keep. Keep the FNV derivation, if it is wanted at all, only as a tiebreaker seeded with that per-attempt nonce. Cover it with a DB cell: answer `mia`=X, answer `mia`=Y, answer `mia`=X again, and assert the third call succeeds and the item reads X.

findings.what: A reconciliation that adds nothing still rotates the CAS token and appends a snapshot, so a second press of "Start firm setup" (a different op key) stales every in-flight editor for no state change.
findings.evidence: Probe on 55607/clara_648r: `L4 no-op reseed bumped revision 2 -> 3 | an in-flight answer then -> CLR06/stale_plan`; and under concurrency two simultaneous seeds both succeed (`P4b seed race -> ok seeded=0 | ok seeded=12 | items: 12 | revisions: 3`). The concurrency storm found no lock-order defect at all — 30 concurrent seed/answer/defer/commit calls produced only `ok` and `CLR06`, zero `40P01`, zero CHECK inconsistencies, exactly one live `reporting_framework` record and a revision counter matching the snapshot count.
findings.fix: Skip the bump when `v_added = 0` (return the unchanged plan in the receipt), or keep it and say so in `seed.help`. Not a correctness problem either way.

findings.what: For a firm that holds no firm-scope plan at all, `get_firm_setup` still returns twelve items, `counter.required_total = 8` and eight `required_outstanding` keys — a progress reading for a plan that does not exist.
findings.evidence: Probe on 55607/clara_648r: `S2 no-plan envelope: {"plan_id":null,"state":null,"seeded":false,"items":12,"counter":{"required_total":8,"required_answered":0},"outstanding":8,"facts":0}`; `S2 seed on a planless firm -> CLR11`. Harmless today because both consumers check `plan_id === null` first (firm-setup-checklist.tsx:305-308, firm-setup-tile.tsx:40-41).
findings.fix: Return a zeroed counter and an empty `required_outstanding` when `p.id is null`, so no consumer can ever paint progress for an absent plan.

findings.what: `confirmed_facts` filters on `r.superseded_at is null` only (no `state = 'live'`), so a withdrawn record stays in "Facts confirmed in setup" forever and `facts.empty` can never return once anything has been withdrawn.
findings.evidence: Probe on 55607/clara_648r: `P7 withdraw -> ok | record: {"state":"superseded","superseded_at":"…"}` and then `P7 confirmed_facts after withdraw: [["default_currency","withdrawn"]] | item.knowledge_record_id: null` — the withdrawal tombstone is the surviving row. The panel does badge it (`facts.withdrawn`, firm-confirmed-facts-panel.tsx:101) and blocks correction (`facts.notCorrectable`), so this is a legibility choice rather than a defect; it is unstated in the file header and untested.
findings.fix: Either state the intent in §F's header and add a cell asserting a withdrawn fact keeps rendering with its badge, or exclude `state = 'withdrawn'` and let the item fall back to pending-for-recapture (which F1's control would then reach).

findings.what: The branch deviates from brief merge-risk 2 ("one `SCOPE_ENTRANCES` row for `/settings/setup`") and the deviation is correct — I checked it rather than taking the report's word.
findings.evidence: `SCOPE_ENTRANCES` holds exactly four entries and every one is a layout or an API route (`app/(firm)/layout.tsx`, `app/(full)/layout.tsx`, `app/api/runtime/[...path]/route.ts`, `app/api/build-info/route.ts`) — there are no per-page rows, so adding one for a page under `app/(firm)` would have made it a fifth entrance. Final-report assumption #5 is verified. Also verified clean: zero `create or replace` and zero foreign `alter table` in 0203 (so none of DECISIONS §1.3's assigned recuts is touched and no pre-image sha pin is owed), `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat -- packages/runtime` and `-- .github` both empty (no Workflow, no World leg, no `db-live-gates` row — the ticket promises none), `node scripts/check-frozen-workflows.mjs` OK (281 files), `packages/runtime/scripts/check-parts-parity.mjs` OK, no view and no masked human-read path added, FORCE RLS on the one new table, and full tenant/machine isolation (firm B reads 0 rows of firm A's plan items and knowledge records; `clara_agent_ro`/`clara_runtime`/both wake roles get 42501 on all three surfaces; `clara_authenticated` gets 42501 on every direct DML including `onboarding_plan_items`; the catalogue refuses owner UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE with CLR08).
findings.fix: No change. Record the deviation in the ticket's evidence so the merge-prep step does not re-add the row.
